content.text:
Links containing other links now render as the spec requires. `[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)` gives `

[foo bar](/uri)

`. The reference form `[foo [bar](/uri)][ref]` is handled the same way. The spec suite passes (1781 tests, 0 failures) and so do the 44 unit tests. I didn't run `tsc`, so the type changes are unchecked. I also didn't render any of the report's example strings directly. A permission denial blocked my one-off script, so the spec tests are the check for examples 518, 519 and 532. **Cause:** `outputLink` in `src/Tokenizer.ts` built a link token and tokenized its text without checking whether the text itself produced a link. **Fix:** after tokenizing the text, `outputLink` now checks for a link token at any depth. If it finds one, it returns just the opening `[` as plain text. The lexer then carries on and parses the inner link normally. The check applies only to links, so images inside links, and links inside image alt text, still work as before. I also made `outputLink` restore the previous `inLink` state instead of resetting it to `false`. **Spec fixtures:** examples 518, 519 and 532 were marked `shouldFail` in `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`. They pass now, so I removed those flags. Re-serializing the JSON also reformatted a few other lines in both files (9 lines changed in each). I didn't add a separate unit test, since the spec examples cover this case.
